description: Team FLARE is developing health monitoring software to protect astronauts during space missions by detecting health risks and providing timely alerts. FLARE symbolizes a lifeline in critical situations. We welcome team members interested in programming, AI, healthcare, data analysis, UI/UX design, and research. Bring your creativity, curiosity, teamwork, and problem-solving skills to help make space exploration safer!
summary:
FLARE (Flight Life Assessment & Response Engine) is a space-mission crew health and safety platform that brings astronaut wellbeing information and emergency-response training into one place. Space missions expose crew members to demanding conditions, isolation and limited access to medical support. FLARE helps users review key aspects of crew readiness through a central dashboard.

The platform includes crew profiles and mission information; health tracking for heart rate, heart-rate variability and blood oxygen saturation; sleep records; wellbeing check-ins for mood, stress and fatigue; and reaction-time testing. Configurable alerts flag readings that cross demonstration thresholds, while historical views and reports help users review recorded information. FLARE also includes device-management interfaces and data backup and import options.

A distinctive feature is its interactive crisis simulation. The user becomes an onboard medical officer responding to a fictional astronaut injured during an EVA. They manage oxygen and medical resources, monitor vital signs, assess injuries and decide whether to stabilise the astronaut on the station or request an emergency return to Earth. The scenario encourages prioritisation and decision-making under pressure.

FLARE aims to support astronaut health awareness, crew readiness and emergency preparedness. It is a prototype: data is simulated or manually entered, and the application is not a medical device or source of medical guidance.
details:
FLARE is an innovative astronaut health-monitoring and mission-safety platform designed to support the physical health, mental wellbeing, performance and emergency preparedness of astronauts during space missions.

Space exploration is one of humanity's greatest achievements, but travelling beyond Earth comes with serious challenges. Astronauts work in isolated environments where medical resources are limited, communication with Earth can be delayed, and even a small health problem can become a major mission risk.

FLARE was developed to address these challenges by bringing essential crew-health information and emergency training into one integrated platform.

The application provides a centralised dashboard where mission teams can manage crew members, monitor important health indicators, review sleep patterns, track psychological wellbeing and assess performance through reaction-time tests. It monitors key indicators such as heart rate (HR), heart-rate variability (HRV) and blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), while maintaining historical records that help users understand changes over time.

Beyond physical health, FLARE recognises that an astronaut's mental condition is equally important. Its wellbeing module allows crew members to record their mood, stress and fatigue levels, while guided breathing exercises offer an opportunity to practise relaxation. Its sleep-monitoring and performance-tracking features provide further insight into factors that can influence astronaut readiness.

Another important feature is its configurable alert system, which identifies readings that cross defined thresholds and organises alerts according to severity. This helps bring attention to potentially concerning information and supports further review by qualified personnel.

What makes FLARE particularly distinctive is its interactive space-medical emergency simulation. In this scenario, users take the role of an onboard medical officer responsible for an injured astronaut following a micrometeoroid incident during an extravehicular activity. They must manage oxygen, control bleeding, investigate injuries, monitor vital signs and make critical decisions with limited medical resources. Ultimately, they must decide whether the astronaut can be stabilised onboard or requires an emergency return to Earth. This creates an engaging training experience that demonstrates the importance of preparation, resource management and decision-making under pressure.

FLARE also includes crew management, mission information, device-management interfaces, historical data visualisation, activity logs, customisable settings and downloadable reports in PDF, CSV and JSON formats.

Our vision is to make astronaut health and safety an essential part of future space exploration. We aim to develop FLARE further through real wearable-device integration, secure data synchronisation, advanced health-trend analysis and improved emergency decision-support capabilities.

FLARE is more than a health-monitoring concept. It is a mission-focused approach to understanding astronaut wellbeing, preparing for emergencies and supporting the people who make space exploration possible.

Our MissionProtect the Humans Behind Space Exploration.

FLARE — Because every successful mission begins with the safety of its crew.

Key project highlights

  • Purpose: Astronaut health, wellbeing and mission safety.
  • Innovation: Combining crew monitoring with interactive emergency medical training.
  • Technology: Interactive digital dashboard, data visualisation, configurable alerts and reporting.
  • Impact: Supporting awareness, preparedness and informed crew-health decisions.
  • Future potential: Real wearable integration and more advanced health analytics.

Technical transparency: FLARE is currently a prototype using simulated and manually entered data stored in browser local storage. It is not a certified medical device, and its alerts are not medical diagnoses.
